version: "2"

linters:
  default: standard        # errcheck, govet, ineffassign, staticcheck, unused — and nothing else
  enable:
    # security: gosec is NOT in the standard group and has to be named.
    - gosec
    # correctness, firing today

    - usetesting
    # correctness, zero findings today, real targets in W2-W5
    - bodyclose
    - rowserrcheck
    - sqlclosecheck
    - asasalint
    - bidichk
    - copyloopvar
    - durationcheck
    - gocheckcompilerdirectives
    - makezero
    - misspell
    - nilerr
    - nilnesserr
    - nolintlint
    - predeclared
    - reassign
    - recvcheck
    - unconvert
    - wastedassign

  settings:
    errcheck:
      check-type-assertions: true
    govet:
      # NOT enable-all: it turns on `shadow` (23 findings, all the repository's own
      # `if err := f(); err != nil` idiom) and `fieldalignment` (12) — both of which upstream's own
      # vet suite omits as too noisy.
      enable:
        - nilness
        - unusedwrite
    gosec:
      excludes:
        - G104                      # duplicates errcheck exactly
    nolintlint:
      allow-unused: false
      require-explanation: true
      require-specific: true
    rowserrcheck:
      packages:
        - github.com/jackc/pgx/v5   # the default only knows database/sql
    staticcheck:
      checks:
        - all
    # No misspell.locale: US flags the repository's British prose, UK flags Go's own vocabulary,
    # and the neutral default flags neither.

  exclusions:
    generated: lax
    warn-unused: true
    rules:
      # wasm32 ABI: every pointer and length crossing the wazero boundary is a uint32 by
      # construction. Scoped to this package, NOT global — G115 must stay live in internal/cborx,
      # which parses untrusted envelope bytes.
      - path: ^internal/mlswasi/
        text: G115
        linters:
          - gosec
      - path: _test\.go$
        linters:
          - errcheck
          - gosec

formatters:
  enable:
    - gofmt
    - goimports
  settings:
    goimports:
      local-prefixes:               # a LIST in v2, not the v1 string
        - github.com/jonasthim/dilla

issues:
  # The defaults (50 / 3 / true) silently drop real findings.
  max-issues-per-linter: 0
  max-same-issues: 0
  uniq-by-line: false

## Follow-up cards (not in this plan)

Work this plan deliberately leaves undone, each with the reason it is not v1 and the shape the fix
would take. None of them blocks a task below.

1. **`device_list_entries` wasi export** — invariant 4's clause "its DSK is in the newest signed
   device list" is enforced through `ds.DeviceLists`, which fails closed for every user until the
   export exists (NV-B8, task 20). The fix is one additive export,
   `device_list_entries([abi, blob, ssk_pub]) -> [0, [[dsk_pub, revoked]]]`, wrapping
   `dilla_core::identity::device_list::verify`, plus the Go host binding. A substring search over
   the serialized blob is not membership and is not written.
2. **Interaction groups (opcode 33)** — `interaction` is in the frame catalogue, the codec and
   `frames.json` (task 17), but no task in either plan produces one, and an interaction group has no
   `channel_id`, so the blob routes cannot address it (NV-B3; Plan 2's card 1 carries the storage
   half). Needs either a synthetic channel row per interaction group or a group-scoped surface with
   its own ACL.
3. **Unicode handles** — v1 refuses non-ASCII handles because no maintained Go UTS #39 confusables
   implementation exists (facts-auth §6.1, R16, task 8). The card is "adopt a confusables table and
   a skeleton-collision check", not "loosen the regexp".
4. **Moderator deletion of an end-to-end-encrypted message** — R29 makes deletion uploader-only at
   v1 (task 23). The capability an operator will ask for is a signed moderation event the DS can
   verify without reading plaintext; shared with Plan 2's cards 2 and 8.
5. **One franking implementation** — `ds.FrankingTag` (task 23) and Plan 2 task 17's
   `api.Commitment`/`api.Tag` compute the same two `protocol/04` equations in two packages with two
   spellings. `protocol/vectors/franking.json` keeps them honest; the right shape is one
   `internal/frank` package both import. Parked behind W5's DS API freeze, because moving
   `ds.FrankingTag` touches the commit path.
6. **The client library** — `testkit/src/ds/remote.rs` (task 28) is a real DS client over the real
   frames and is the seed of the client library R14 names, but it is synchronous, loopback-only and
   TLS-free by design. Promoting it is its own wave.
7. **Client-side backup routes `/v1/backups/*`** — task 10 of Plan 2 ships the `backups` table and
   `store.OpsBackups`; the four client-facing routes are spec line 653 W11 work and are in neither
   plan (Plan 2's P2-4).

## Assembly notes

This file was assembled on 2026-09-24 from two independently drafted parts — tasks 0–13 (part 1a)
and tasks 14–30 (part 1b) — against the binding contract `interfaces.md`. The task bodies are
**verbatim**; the changes made while assembling are listed here, each with what proves it.

1. **Task headings normalised.** Part 1a wrote `### Task N — <name> · part 1a`; part 1b wrote
   `### Task N: <name>`. All fourteen 1a headings are rewritten to `### Task N: <name>`. Nothing
   else in those lines changed, and no cross-reference in either part cites a heading by its
   punctuation.
2. **Numbering is already continuous.** Part 1a ends at task 13 and part 1b starts at task 14
   (`interfaces.md` §10: "Plan 1 tasks are numbered 0–30 continuously across parts 1a and 1b"), so
   no task was renumbered. **Task 27a keeps its letter**: it is the wiring task between 27 and 28,
   and tasks 17–30 cross-reference "task 27a" by name in prose, test names and commit subjects.
   Renumbering it to 28 would have silently invalidated those references and shifted 28–30.
3. **One migration number corrected.** Task 23's Files block wrote
   `internal/store/{sqlite,postgres}/migrations/00005_messages.sql`, which contradicts part 1b's own
   deviation **B19** ("plan-1a lands exactly `00001_init.sql`; part 1b lands `00002_mls.sql` and
   `00003_messages.sql`") and task 19's `00002_mls.sql`. Rewritten to `00003_messages.sql` (one
   occurrence). The goose sequence this plan lands is therefore `00001_init.sql`,
   `00002_mls.sql`, `00003_messages.sql`, and Plan 2 allocates from `00004`.
4. **No call-site rewriting was needed inside Plan 1.** Part 1b's deviation B12 already pins every
   `internal/server` call to the spellings part 1a task 6 produces (`DecodeBody(w, r, max, v)`,
   `WriteError(w, err)`, `Errorf(code Code, …)`, `auth.FromContext`), and a scan of the assembled
   file finds no `server.SessionOf`, `server.WriteCBOR`, `server.WriteError(w, r, …)` or
   `server.Errorf(http.Status…` call outside the prose of deviations ID14 and B12, which quote the
   wrong spellings in order to forbid them.
5. **In-task back-references are kept as written.** Task 2 step "write `00001_init.sql`" shows
   `<the full text of 001_instance.sql>` and three siblings: those are the four schema files the
   same task wrote four steps earlier, concatenated between the goose markers, and the step spells
   out the concatenation order and the reverse drop order. They are not placeholders — no content is
   deferred to a later task or to the reader's judgement.
6. **The four cross-part items are settled (controller, 2026-09-24).** They could not be settled
   from `interfaces.md`, were recorded rather than guessed, and the controller has since ruled on
   each. What both plans now say:
   - **`store.Repository`'s embed list.** Deviation ID1 (task 3) requires "an explicit numbered step
     that edits the embed list and shows the exact new `type Repository interface { … }` text".
     **Task 19 step 1a** adds `MLS`, **task 23 step 1a** adds `Messages` and `Cursors`, and
     **Plan 2 task 1 step 9** adds `Structure` (its tasks 8 and 10 then add `Readable`, `Blobs`
     and `OpsBackups` — P2-D23). Each of those steps shows the whole new declaration and ends in
     `go build ./...` plus `go test ./internal/store/...`; without them `tx.CreateGroup(ctx, row)`
     on a `store.Repository` does not compile and the task's own "run it and watch it pass" step
     fails.
   - **Plan 2's migration base.** One sequence across both plans: Plan 1 lands `00001_init.sql`,
     `00002_mls.sql`, `00003_messages.sql` (note 3 above, deviation B19) and **Plan 2 allocates
     from `00004` upward in the order its tasks run** — `00004_structure.sql`, `00005_channels.sql`,
     `00006_overwrites.sql`, `00007_bans.sql`, `00008_channel_members.sql`, `00009_readable.sql`,
     `00010_blobs.sql`, `00011_voice.sql`, `00012_reports.sql`. Plan 2's preamble, every concrete
     filename, every `goose` invocation and every `ls` expectation in it now read that way, and
     both plans' "list the directory first" steps remain the safety net.
   - **`server.MaxBody`.** There is no such constant and task 6 does not gain one: it already
     produces the helper, `server.DecodeBody(w, r, max int64, v any)`, and `interfaces.md` §5.3
     fixes the value at the call site (64 KiB on every CBOR route but `/v1/groups/{id}/message`,
     which is `max_ciphertext_bytes + 4096`, and the two 96 KiB envelope routes). Plan 2 passes the
     number; its P2-1 row, its contract section and its assembly note 4 now say so, and the name
     `server.MaxBody` appears nowhere in it.
   - **Codes Plan 2 needs.** They are **this plan's**, not Plan 2's: task 0's table is **25 rows**
     and task 6's constants carry `E_ENVELOPE_SHAPE`, `E_ENVELOPE_TYPE`, `E_ENVELOPE_LIMIT`
     (all 400, mirroring the Rust envelope module's codes and the vector corpus) and
     `E_CHANNEL_MODE` (**403** — the operation is not allowed for the channel's mode). Plan 2's
     P2-D30 records that it consumes them rather than adding them, and its task 9 uses
     `server.CodeEnvelopeShape`, `CodeEnvelopeType`, `CodeEnvelopeLimit` and `CodeChannelMode`
     instead of code strings. `scripts/check-protocol-docs.mjs` (task 0 step 15) diffs the 25 rows
     against `internal/server/errors.go` in both directions, so the two sides cannot drift.

   "Needs verification" tables are the parts' own text.
